channel.title: Otago Daily Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Otago Daily Times (odt.co.nz)

item.title: Driver bypasses alcohol interlock for tipsy highway jaunt
item.description: Photo: ODT files An allegedly drunk woman was seen driving erratically while towing a caravan after managing to bypass her vehicle's alcohol interlock, police say.

item.title: Beach where mayor went for dip unsafe
item.description: Wellington's south coast beaches have been rated unsuitable for swimming just two days after the city's mayor went for a swim in Lyall Bay to show it was safe.

item.title: Festival to be electric opportunity
item.description: Timaru-born musician Caitlin Bradley (CAITLIN) will be performing on the main stage at Electric Avenue on Saturday. PHOTO: SUPPLIED A Timaru-born musician is set to take to the main stage at the biggest festival in Australasia this weekend.

item.title: Surge in traffic delivers increased profits
item.description: Jetstar and Air New Zealand launched new returns flights from Christchurch to Hamilton. PHOTOS: CHRISTCHURCH AIRPORT A surge in air traffic has propelled Christchurch Airport to deliver a 24% increase in first-half profit to $29.5 million.

item.title: New science institute culling 134 jobs
item.description: Bioeconomy Science Institute chief executiver Mark Piper. Photo: SUPPLIED/PLANT & FOOD RESEARCH (file) The government's Bioeconomy Science Institute is to cut 134 jobs less than a year after it was formed.

item.title: 'Phew': Kath and Kim star announces cancer remission
item.description: Beloved Australian comedian Magda Szubanski says she is breathing a sigh of relief after announcing her rare blood cancer is in remission.

item.title: Pair charged after woman's body found at worksite
item.description: Photo: RNZ Two Napier men have been charged in connection with the homicide of a Rotorua woman whose body was found at a worksite.

item.title: Subjects cancelled, untrained teachers hired, say principals
item.description: Photo: ODT files By John Gerritsen of RNZ Secondary principals say the worsening shortage of teachers is forcing schools to cancel subjects and hire untrained teachers.

item.title: 'National security threat' identified
item.description: Ronndog Keefe pleaded guilty to 13 charges, including distributing objectionable child exploitation material and threatening to kill. Photo: Open Justice Warning: This article discusses issues of child sexual exploitation and mass killing and may be distressing for some people. A Hawke's Bay man who distributed "repugnant" videos and images showing the sexual abuse of children, and who was dubbed a national security threat by police for planning a mass killing, can now be publicly identified.
